usage: sf-mod-check diff <old> <new> [--data <Data folder>] [--json] [--out <file>] [--all] [--quiet] [--verbose] [--log <file>]
         <old> and <new> are two plugins (.esm .esp .esl), or two mods: each a .zip, .7z or .rar download or a folder.
         Plugins in two mods are paired by file name; one in only one of them is listed as added or removed.
         The report counts records per type, names the fields that changed (with each changed value, a
         reordered list and dropped translations named under the record), groups placed objects by cell, and
         lists leveled-list entries added and removed and base-object swaps. For two mods it also compares the
         loose files (by SHA-256), each archive's files (paired by name) and the objects, states and functions of
         changed scripts (.pex; names only, never code).
         --data      the game's Data folder, for the EditorIDs of records in the masters (default: Steam's usual folder)
         --json      the report as JSON instead of text (always complete); on stdout the RESULT line follows
                     the JSON, so use --out for a file that holds only the JSON
         --out       write the report to this file (stdout then gets only the RESULT line)
         --all       list everything in the text report (long lists are cut short otherwise), and each cell's records
         Records whose bytes differ but whose fields are all equal count as noise, which is no difference.
         Scripts and script properties are matched by name, so a new order alone is noise.
         exit 0 = no real differences (noise only counts as none), 1 = differences, 2 = bad input or setup

usage: sf-mod-check gap <plugin> [--data <Data folder>] [--masters-dir <folder>]... [--quiet] [--verbose] [--log <file>]
         Compares every record the plugin overrides with its master's copy and reports what the Mutagen library
         0.54.4 is known to lose when it writes a plugin (ERROR), any other field the master has and the plugin
         lacks (WARNING; it may be on purpose), and overridden placed references missing from the ONAM list.
         Masters are looked for in the plugin's own folder, then each --masters-dir in order, then --data.
         --data         the game's Data folder (default: Steam's usual folder)
         --masters-dir  another folder to look for masters in (can be given more than once)
         --quiet        no byline, and no WARNING lines when there are errors
         --verbose, --log <file>  the troubleshooting log on stderr, or in that file
         The last line is RESULT: OK (0 errors, n warnings), RESULT: FAIL (n errors, n warnings) or RESULT: CANNOT CHECK (...).
         exit 0 = no errors (warnings allowed), 1 = errors, 2 = can't check (a missing plugin or master, a bad argument)

            main fields; --json adds it as "tree". On a dialogue topic (DIAL) it also lists the topic's lines
            (INFOs): each one's winner and each response's number, text, emotion and face fields ("infos").
            A sound GUID (SoundReference, WWED) also prints in the form a Wwise bank manifest uses

usage: sf-mod-check lines <EditorID | FormKey | FormID> [--plugins <Plugins.txt> | --mo2 <MO2 folder> [--profile <name>]]
                          [--data <Data folder>] [--extra-data <folder>] [--compare <NPC>] [--type <name>] [--max <n>]
                          [--no-files] [--json] [--quiet] [--verbose] [--log <file>]
       sf-mod-check lines <EditorID | FormKey> --plugin <plugin file> [--masters-dir <folder>]... [...]
  Lists the dialogue lines one NPC can speak, grouped by type (the topic's Category / Subtype, for example
  Combat / Hit), and counts them per type. A line counts when its speaker is the NPC, a condition names the NPC
  (GetIsID) or an alias it fills (GetIsAliasRef), or a scene gives the line to an alias the NPC fills. Lines for
  the NPC's voice type (GetIsVoiceType) are listed apart as shared lines. Each line says whether its voice file
  (wem) and lip file (lip, .ffxanim) are there, in the plugin's archives or loose.
  The NPC      an EditorID (letter case ignored), a FormKey (005788:Starfield.esm) or a console FormID (00005788)
               (an EditorID of exactly 8 hex digits: put eid: before it, as eid:00005788)
  --plugin     read only this plugin and its masters (found in its folder, then each --masters-dir, then --data)
  --compare    count another NPC's lines per type too (for example a vanilla companion) and mark the types this
               NPC has none of as missing; the same forms as the NPC
  --type       keep only lines of this Category (Combat) or Category / Subtype ("Combat / Hit"); letter case ignored
  --max        list at most this many lines (default 200; 0 lists them all); the counts are always complete
  --no-files   don't look for the voice and lip files (faster; wem and lip show ?)
  --json       print one JSON object with every line
Exit 0 = the NPC was found (even with no lines), 1 = not found, 2 = could not run.

usage: sf-mod-check scenes <NPC or quest: EditorID | FormKey | FormID> [--plugins <Plugins.txt> | --mo2 <MO2 folder> [--profile <name>]]
                           [--data <Data folder>] [--extra-data <folder>] [--hub <scene>] [--out <file.md>] [--json] [--max <n>]
                           [--quiet] [--verbose] [--log <file>]
       sf-mod-check scenes <EditorID | FormKey> --plugin <plugin file> [--masters-dir <folder>]... [...]
  Prints an NPC's or a quest's conversations (scenes) as a tree: each part's lines, the player's choices and the
  NPC's answers, and where the talk goes next. Then it checks them: a line that jumps to a part a scene doesn't
  have, choices with no way out, stages that are needed but never set (or set but never checked), and Scene topics
  no scene uses. Last comes a table of each quest's stages: the author's note, what sets it and what needs it.
  The NPC or quest  an EditorID (letter case ignored), a FormKey (000803:MyMod.esm) or a console FormID
                    (an EditorID of exactly 8 hex digits: put eid: before it, as eid:00005788)
  --plugin     read only this plugin and its masters, and show only the scenes the plugin adds or changes
  --hub        the talk menu scene (EditorID or FormKey), when the one found by counting jumps is wrong
  --out        write the tree to this Markdown file and print only the counts
  --max        show at most this many scenes (default 50; 0 shows them all); the problems and stages are always complete
  --json       print one JSON object instead
Exit 0 = found (even with problems), 1 = not found, 2 = could not run.

result.stdout:
usage: sf-mod-check voice-lines <plugin> [--out <file>] [--voice <voice type EditorID>]... [--utf8]
                                [--data <Data folder>] [--masters-dir <folder>]... [--quiet] [--verbose] [--log <file>]
  Writes the plugin's voiced dialogue lines as a tab-separated file in the Creation Kit dialogue-export columns
  that voice tools read, one row per voice type and file number:
    VOICE TYPE  FILENAME  RESPONSE TEXT  FACE  SCRIPT NOTES  SEX  FULL PATH  INFO  RESPONSE
  A line's voice types come from the first of these that names an NPC or a voice type: its own conditions
  (GetIsID, GetIsVoiceType; each alternative of an OR counts), its speaker (the line's Speaker, or the NPC that
  fills its alias or scene alias), its dialogue group's conditions, its quest's. --voice covers lines with none.
  Player lines and lines that link a SharedDialog line are left out.
  <plugin>        the plugin file; its masters are found in its folder, then each --masters-dir, then --data
  --out           write the list to this file (default: the screen, stdout)
  --voice         a voice type (EditorID) for the lines that name none; may be given more than once
  --utf8          write UTF-8 (default: Windows-1252, what the Creation Kit writes and Voice Cloner reads;
                  a UTF-8 file needs SVC_EXPORT_ENCODING=utf-8 set on the Voice Cloner side)
Exit 0 = written (even with no rows), 2 = could not run. Messages and the RESULT line go to stderr.

  <plugin>        the plugin file; its masters are found in its folder, then each --masters-dir, then --data
  --out           write the list to this file (default: the screen, stdout)
  --voice         a voice type (EditorID) for the lines that name none; may be given more than once

  --force     overwrite files that already exist (default: an existing file is left alone and reported)
  --max-size  the most the files may add up to, in GB (default 2). Checked before anything is written.
File names that would leave --out (.., rooted, drive or network paths, reserved Windows names) are refused.

failed, 2 = could not run (no archive, damaged archive, nothing matched, texture archive, over --max-size).

usage: sf-mod-check edit <plugin> --out <new plugin> [--drop-master <master>] [--set-light]
                         [--set-text <INFO or MESG> --text "<new text>" [--response <n>]]...
                         [--data <Data folder>] [--masters-dir <folder>]... [--json] [--quiet] [--verbose] [--log <file>]
  Makes a few safe changes to a finished plugin and writes them to a NEW file. The plugin itself is never changed.
  The new file is kept only when three proofs pass on it: diff (only the intended changes), gap (no new loss) and
  check (no new ERROR). Otherwise it is deleted, and the proof that failed says why.
  --out          the new plugin file; it must not exist yet, and it can't be the input
  --drop-master  remove a master the plugin doesn't use (the FormIDs after it are renumbered); refused if anything uses it
  --set-light    set the light flag; refused unless the plugin is full and its own records are 000800 to 000FFF
  --set-text     replace one line's text: an INFO's response text (NAM1) or a MESG's description (DESC), named by
                 EditorID, FormKey (000801:MyMod.esm) or console FormID. Give the new text with --text after it,
                 and --response <n> for an INFO's other responses (numbered from 1, as `find --full` shows them).
                 Repeat --set-text for more records (one line per record in a run). A localized plugin is
                 refused (its text is in .STRINGS files).
  --data         the game's Data folder, for the masters (default: Steam's usual folder)
  --masters-dir  look for masters here first (default: the plugin's own folder), then in the Data folder
  --json         print one JSON object: the edits, each proof's result and whether the new file was kept
  --quiet        leave out the tool's name and version line
  --verbose      also print the log (each step and proof in detail) to stderr
  --log <file>   write that log to a file, for a bug report
Exit 0 = the new file was kept, 1 = a proof failed (nothing kept), 2 = refused or could not run.
